prediction.likelyOutcome: McCarthy is unlikely to collect the full $176,691.71 (or even the $145,706.56 lien amount) given the undisputed change-order-clause violation and the admittedly erroneous, repeatedly-revised invoicing; expect a trimmed award closer to the value of actually-used, contract-rate material. Stark has a solid, well-documented wrongful-lien/slander-of-title counterclaim worth at least ~$7,600 in hard costs (plus a plausible but unquantified lost-interest claim on the $265,037.55 collateral deposit), which substantially offsets whatever residual balance McCarthy recovers, and Stark has a real shot at prevailing-party attorney fees that could flip his net position favorably.

outcome.description: After a seven-day bench trial the district court dismissed McCarthy's lien-foreclosure and contract claims and awarded Stark $51,760.83 on his breach-of-contract counterclaim (completion cost of $202,090.81 less $150,329.98 unpaid contract balance) plus $34,100.46 in ICPA damages (total $85,861.29), and $129,434 in attorney fees and $4,535.33 costs. The Idaho Supreme Court affirmed in full and awarded Stark fees on appeal.
